macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks end volatile week lower as oil prices rise
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.23% to 52,215.16, the S&P 500 dropped 0.52% to 7,623.68, and the Nasdaq Composite declined 0.21% to 25,955.34. Rising oil prices, inflation concerns, and skepticism over heavy artificial-intelligence investment pressured sentiment.[1]

items.title: Fed expected to hold rates next week amid possible December hike
items.summary: Markets broadly expect the Federal Reserve to leave interest rates unchanged at its upcoming meeting, while investors will watch for signals about a potential quarter-point hike in December.[1][2]

items.title: U.S. economic data shows resilient manufacturing but slower services growth
items.summary: The flash U.S. manufacturing PMI rose to 56.0 in October, a 53-month high, while the services PMI eased to 57.9 from 58.8 in September. Cost pressures remained a concern.[2]

items.title: Oil prices surge as Middle East risks intensify inflation concerns
items.summary: Crude prices climbed sharply, with Brent reaching a five-month high and U.S. crude moving above $100 a barrel as markets assessed possible disruptions linked to escalating Middle East tensions.[6][10]

items.title: American Express raises outlook while announcing workforce cuts
items.summary: American Express lifted its profit forecast but said it plans to eliminate about 5% of its workforce; its shares fell during Friday’s trading.[1]

items.title: SLB shares rise after earnings beat
items.summary: Oilfield-services provider SLB gained 7% after reporting third-quarter profit above Wall Street expectations.[1]

items.title: Major technology earnings loom next week
items.summary: Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon are among the major companies scheduled to report earnings, with investors focused on artificial-intelligence-related capital spending and profitability.[1][6]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $81,000 after sharp decline
items.summary: Bitcoin fell 3.2% to about $80,840 before recovering to roughly $81,700. Crypto markets recorded approximately $336 million in liquidations, including $281 million in long positions.

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs see $635 million in daily outflows
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $635 million in net outflows, their largest single-day drawdown since late June, adding selling pressure to the market.

items.title: Initia halts blockchain after reported $2.6 million exploit
items.summary: The Initia layer-1 blockchain and its rollups were suspended after researchers reported an exploit that allegedly enabled unauthorized token minting and drained more than $2.6 million in crypto assets.

items.title: SEC adds tokenization to examination priorities
items.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission identified tokenized securities as an emerging market risk in its fiscal 2027 examination priorities, alongside areas including quantum computing and extended trading hours.

items.title: OCC finalizes stablecoin issuer rules
items.summary: The U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency finalized rules addressing stablecoin reserves, redemptions and related services, with issuer approval requirements generally beginning January 18, 2027.

items.title: Upbit listing sends BMT sharply higher
items.summary: BMT rose more than 50% following news that South Korean exchange Upbit would list the token, pushing its market capitalization to approximately $20 million.

items.title: Institution moves AAVE and WLD to exchanges
items.summary: An institution that had been inactive for more than a year transferred 156,690 AAVE and 19.74 million WLD, with roughly $18.8 million of the assets reportedly deposited on exchanges for potential sale.

items.title: Crypto prediction-market trading reaches record volume
items.summary: Crypto-related contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket generated a reported $2.7 billion in notional volume during the past week, as short-term Bitcoin up-or-down contracts gained popularity.

items.title: Kazakhstan court bars six exchanges from unlicensed AIFC services
items.summary: The Astana International Financial Centre court issued injunctions preventing Coinbase, BingX, HTX, BitMart, WEEX and Bitcoin.com from providing or advertising digital-asset services in the centre without authorization.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Moonshot launches Kimi K3.1 Pro with tighter hacking controls
items.summary: Moonshot introduced Kimi K3.1 Pro, an open-weight model in the 3-trillion-parameter class that the company describes as its most capable model. The release includes restrictions intended to reduce its ability to assist with hacking amid concerns about AI-enabled cyberattacks.

items.title: OpenAI moves frontier-model training offline after security incident
items.summary: OpenAI said it will train its most advanced models without live internet access, instead using cached or indexed web data. The change follows a September incident involving a research model that gained limited internet access through a configuration error.

items.title: Block unveils Dessa speech-to-speech model
items.summary: Block announced Dessa, a speech-to-speech model it says was trained from scratch on human conversations and can run on a MacBook Pro with an M4 Max chip. Initial access is limited to a small group of AI safety researchers.

items.title: Anthropic and Theorem use Claude to verify open-source code
items.summary: Anthropic and Theorem reportedly used Claude to formally verify code from 123 open-source libraries, generating roughly 180 million lines of proof code. The effort identified hundreds of errors and highlighted potential applications for auditable AI-assisted software testing.

items.title: Canva introduces Craft image-generation model
items.summary: Canva launched Craft, an image model reportedly trained on design templates that supports generation across more than 30 aspect ratios and text in 55 languages.

items.title: Stanford, Together, and Emory researchers develop self-organizing agent teams
items.summary: Researchers introduced a framework that allows AI agents to learn collaborative strategies dynamically. Reported tests found the teams outperformed individual models on complex mathematics and physics problems.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Arkane Lyon faces possible closure, putting Marvel’s Blade at risk
items.summary: Microsoft is reportedly seeking a buyer or partner for Arkane Lyon under a French labor-law process. The studio could close by November 13 if no deal is reached, potentially jeopardizing Marvel’s Blade and about 217 jobs.

items.title: FIFAe Finals postponed indefinitely
items.summary: The 2026 FIFAe Finals have been postponed until further notice because of regional security developments, including ongoing attacks by Houthi rebels in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Esports World Cup announces 2027 qualifier program
items.summary: The Esports World Cup announced a 2027 qualifier program intended to let tournament organizers and local esports communities run official events on the road to the next World Cup.

items.title: Shigeru Miyamoto to receive Japan’s Order of Culture
items.summary: Nintendo designer Shigeru Miyamoto will receive Japan’s highest cultural honor, becoming the first video game-industry figure recognized with the Order of Culture. The ceremony is scheduled for November 3 at Tokyo’s Imperial Palace.

items.title: Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced to add New Game Plus
items.summary: Ubisoft is reportedly preparing to add the highly requested New Game Plus mode to Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced next week. The remake has reportedly sold more than 3.5 million copies in its first 14 days.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: Apple’s first foldable iPhone sells out amid strong demand
items.summary: Apple’s first foldable iPhone, reportedly called the iPhone Duo, went on sale worldwide on October 23 and quickly sold out of limited in-store inventory, with shipping estimates extending into January in some markets.

items.title: SpaceX explores access to 80,000 U.S. cell sites
items.summary: SpaceX is reportedly negotiating with cellular infrastructure companies for access to at least 80,000 U.S. sites, supporting plans to expand Starlink connectivity and potentially build a major wireless carrier.

items.title: Critical GitLab vulnerability enables unauthenticated code execution
items.summary: A high-impact vulnerability in self-managed GitLab installations reportedly allows unauthenticated attackers to execute code, creating an urgent patching priority for affected organizations.

items.title: U.S. proposes broader restrictions on investment in Chinese technology
items.summary: A proposed Treasury rule would expand limits on U.S. investment in China-related technologies, including quantum computing, advanced chips, supercomputers, hypersonic systems and other technologies tied to national security.
